clue.text: Movement of troops? Record is linked to sudden movements

parts.note: a log is a written record, as a ship's log
tics are sudden involuntary twitches

explanation.surface: A diary entry is tied to jerky twitches.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition's question mark flags that logistics covers far more than moving troops, though military supply and transport is its original sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Logistics is the military science of supplying and transporting forces.

clue.text: Rude words, except about learner's facial care

parts.note: lip is cheeky, insolent talk

indicators.note: the word for 'except' goes about, around, the learner's letter

parts.note: save can mean except, as in 'all save one'
L is the learner driver's plate

explanation.surface: Someone holds back from insults, except when talking about a pupil's skincare.
explanation.definitionFit: Lip salve is a balm applied to the lips, a part of the face, to soothe them.

clue.text: Italian port's good — excellent in retrospect

indicators.note: looking back means the word for excellent is read from right to left

parts.note: A1, read as A ONE, means first-rate

explanation.surface: A tourist praises an Italian harbour town after the visit.
explanation.walkthrough: A1 is a British way of saying first-rate, written out here as A ONE before 'in retrospect' turns it. The 's of 'port's' is 'is', a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Genoa is the major seaport on Italy's Ligurian coast.

clue.text: Intoxicated around pass, drunken Boers? By no means

indicators.note: the word for intoxicated is placed around the mountain pass

parts.note: stoned means high or drunk
a col is a pass between mountains

indicators.note: drunken signals that the letters of Boers are jumbled

explanation.surface: Tipsy South African farmers stagger over a mountain pass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' wraps the word for intoxicated round the pass, and 'drunken' jumbles the farmers. The definition answers the question 'Intoxicated?' with a firm no.
explanation.definitionFit: Asked whether someone is intoxicated, 'by no means' says they are completely clear-headed and without drink.

clue.text: Leaflets in papers? Very popular, sure things, we hear

parts.note: in means fashionable, very popular

indicators.note: we hear tells us the word for sure things is said aloud and spelt by sound

parts.note: certs are certainties, sure bets

explanation.surface: Fashionable newspapers carry flyers that are guaranteed hits.
explanation.walkthrough: CERTS is British racing slang for horses certain to win; said aloud it gives SERTS.
explanation.definitionFit: Inserts are loose advertising leaflets placed inside newspapers and magazines.

clue.text: Dog, quick on the uptake, that is leaping up

parts.note: sharp means mentally quick

indicators.note: in a down clue, leaping up means the letters for 'that is' are read from bottom to top

parts.note: i.e. is the abbreviation for 'id est', that is

explanation.surface: A clever dog bounds upward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaping up' reads the abbreviation for 'that is' upwards, which suits a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: The shar pei is a Chinese breed with a wrinkled coat.

clue.text: Scoundrel curtailed swindle

indicators.note: curtailed means having its tail, the last letter, cut off

parts.note: a scamp is a rascal or rogue

explanation.surface: A rogue has his con trick cut short.
explanation.walkthrough: 'curtailed' takes the last letter P from SCAMP.
explanation.definitionFit: A scam is a dishonest scheme to cheat people.

clue.text: Drink making you race in and out drunkenly

indicators.note: drunkenly signals the letters are staggered into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A tipple that has you lurching in and out of a race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'making you' is link padding; the fodder is RACE IN plus OUT, joined by 'and', and 'drunkenly' rearranges those nine letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Cointreau is a French orange-flavoured liqueur.

clue.text: Being silent about it is this?

definitions.text: Being silent about it is this?

indicators.note: about tells us the word for being silent goes around the contraction

parts.note: mum means silent, as in 'keep mum'
'tis is the poetic contraction of it is

explanation.surface: A riddle asking what quietness amounts to.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts the poetic contraction inside the word for silent; the whole clue then describes the condition it names.
explanation.definitionFit: Mutism is the condition of not speaking, whether chosen or medical.

clue.text: Urgent letters suggesting good protection for battle

definitions.text: Urgent letters suggesting good protection for battle

parts.words: Urgent letters suggesting good protection for battle
parts.note: the priority postal service also reads as top-quality chain armour worn in combat

explanation.surface: A soldier writes home urgently asking for better armour.
explanation.walkthrough: Mail is both post and armour of linked metal rings, so the faster postal service reads as top-grade armour.
explanation.definitionFit: The faster priority postal service carries urgent letters, and the top grade of chain armour protects in combat.

clue.text: Long opening in original Christmas show

parts.note: to long for is to pant for, yearn

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A theatre promises a fresh Christmas production with a lengthy start.
explanation.walkthrough: PANTO is a British pantomime, a family stage comedy put on at Christmas.
explanation.definitionFit: A pantomime is a traditional British festive stage entertainment.

clue.text: Saint surrounding Left -it's disturbed left-winger

indicators.note: disturbed signals that the letters are jumbled

parts.note: the word saint written round L, the abbreviation for left, in any position since the jumble follows
its letters taken as written, apostrophe ignored

explanation.surface: A corrupted radical rants about a stain on the Left.
explanation.walkthrough: The printed 'Taint' cannot supply the letters; reading 'Saint' makes the count work. 'surrounding' sets the saint round L, and 'disturbed' then jumbles all of it with 'it's'.
explanation.definitionFit: A Stalinist follows Stalin's hard-line communism, so is an extreme leftist.

clue.text: Gold Rush initially snared friend, one not normally interested in money

definitions.text: one not normally interested in money

indicators.note: snared means the symbol for gold traps the word for friend inside

parts.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold
a mate is a friend

indicators.note: initially picks the first letter of Rush

explanation.surface: In a gold rush a prospector's pal was caught up in it all for love, not cash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'snared' traps the friend inside the gold symbol, and 'initially' supplies the first letter of Rush; the surface's money theme points at the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An amateur takes part for enjoyment rather than payment.

clue.text: Money some in Europe set aside

indicators.note: some in signals that a part of the following words holds the run of letters

explanation.surface: Funds in parts of Europe are being put by.
explanation.walkthrough: The old currency was set aside when Spain adopted the euro, which the surface nods at.
explanation.definitionFit: The peseta was Spain's currency before the euro.

clue.text: Unpleasant group of people that becomes progressively worse

definitions.meaning: read literally, a nasty clique or set
a chain of cause and effect that feeds on itself

explanation.surface: A nasty clique and a spiral of decline.
explanation.definitionFit: A circle is a social set, and the idiom names a sequence where each problem aggravates the next.

clue.text: Jewel of a part? Hardly

parts.note: a cameo is a carved gem or brooch
a role is a part in a play

explanation.surface: Is this precious stone really a starring part? Hardly.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines too: a gem of a part that is hardly a part at all, a brief appearance.
explanation.definitionFit: A cameo is a tiny appearance by a well-known actor, barely a part.

clue.text: Dress in feathers to eradicate resistance?

parts.note: to wear clothes is to dress in them
down is soft fine feathers

explanation.surface: Putting on a feather coat to beat off opposition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' links; 'Dress in' is one piece, not an insertion signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To wear down opposition is to erode it by persistent pressure.

clue.text: Particularly fitting, as a ruler is?

definitions.meaning: a ruler is literally made for measuring

explanation.surface: A ruler is described as a perfect fit.
explanation.definitionFit: Bespoke clothing is cut for one wearer, and a ruler is manufactured to measure things.

clue.text: What some lace-makers do, left out of gossip

indicators.note: out of signals that the letter is taken away from the word for gossip

parts.note: tattling is idle chattering about others

explanation.surface: Lace workers who chat are excluded from the gossip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left out of' looks like a phrase for being excluded; 'left' is L and 'out of' removes it from TATTLING.
explanation.definitionFit: Tatting is a handmade knotted lace craft done with a shuttle.

clue.text: Man leading navy around very good source of water

indicators.note: leading means the first piece comes before the navy letters
around means the word for man encloses the abbreviation for very

parts.note: a male is a man
RN is the Royal Navy

explanation.surface: A man ahead of the fleet finds a fine spring.
explanation.walkthrough: MALVERN is an English spa town in Worcestershire whose spring water is bottled and sold.
explanation.definitionFit: Malvern's hills feed springs famous for pure bottled drinking water.

clue.text: Dance observed to be a puzzle

parts.note: a jig is a lively folk dance
saw means observed

explanation.surface: A dance someone watched turns out to be baffling.
explanation.definitionFit: A jigsaw is a picture cut into interlocking pieces for reassembly.

clue.text: Make clear indication of golfer's readiness?

definitions.meaning: to resolve or smooth away problems
a golf club taken out of the bag, ready for a shot

explanation.surface: A golfer draws a club from the bag to settle matters.
explanation.definitionFit: To iron out difficulties is to resolve them, and a golfer with a club drawn is set to play.

clue.text: More forceful one involved in unexpected result…

indicators.note: involved in means the numeral letter is placed within the jumbled word
unexpected signals the letters of result are rearranged

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A stronger player is caught up in a shock result.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unexpected' rearranges RESULT and 'involved in' puts I inside; the ellipsis runs the surface on to the next clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Lustier means more vigorous and robust.

clue.text: I had to surmount island's way of speaking

indicators.note: in a down clue, to surmount means to sit on top of the following piece

parts.note: I'd is the contraction of I had
IOM is the Isle of Man abbreviation

explanation.surface: I had to rise above the island's dialect.
explanation.walkthrough: IOM is the Isle of Man, a British Crown dependency in the Irish Sea.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom is a characteristic expression or manner of speech.

clue.text: … result? Twenty nil, reversed before end of game

indicators.note: before means the preceding pieces come ahead of the final letter

parts.note: a score is twenty

indicators.note: reversed means the word nil is read backwards

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: end of picks the last letter

explanation.surface: A match result of twenty-nil overturned before the final whistle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reversed' turns NIL into LIN; 'end of game' gives E.
explanation.definitionFit: A scoreline is the final score of a match.

clue.text: Am I to leave friend from overseas?

parts.note: taken as written
to go is to leave

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether to say goodbye to a foreign pal.
explanation.definitionFit: Amigo is Spanish for a pal, used in English for a companion.

clue.text: Architect's emotional stress, eliminating church

indicators.note: eliminating means the abbreviation for church is removed

parts.note: a wrench is a painful emotional parting

explanation.surface: A designer's anguish over a church being removed.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of 'Architect's' is 'is', a link. Christopher Wren designed St Paul's Cathedral, so a church in the surface misleads.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Christopher Wren was the English designer of St Paul's Cathedral.

clue.text: Chap's information to identify officer recalled

parts.note: gen is British slang for information

indicators.note: recalled means both pieces are read backwards as one run

parts.note: to name someone is to identify them
Lt is lieutenant, an officer

explanation.surface: A fellow's details serve to identify an officer called back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recalled' turns NAMELT into TLEMAN after GEN; the 's of 'Chap's' is 'is', a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A gentleman is a man, a polite word for a fellow.
